target_customer: Bay Area offices with 20 to 1000+ employees buying recurring catered meals and events
problem: Office meals were unhealthy or logistically painful; Zesty offered dietitian-curated menus from local restaurants delivered and served by its own staff.
business_model: B2B corporate catering with markup on restaurant meals and service fees

founders.name: David Langer
founders.background_notes: Left as CEO in July 2016, described as a personal choice; later at Lionheart Ventures per YC page.

founders.name: Chris Hollindale
founders.role: Co-founder, CTO then CEO from July 2016
founders.background_notes: Later built products at Checkr per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Ordering software and menu data were ordinary; the hard part was operations (restaurant sourcing, delivery and on-site service staff), not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Restaurant relationships and a dietitian-curated brand helped, but corporate catering was served by several funded rivals and the service was labor-heavy and copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Square bought Zesty's assets in April 2018 to build Caviar for Teams; about 150 restaurants were in the network and Zesty operated only in the Bay Area.

market_need_then: Startups were signing up: TechCrunch (2014-03) reported Instacart, AngelList, Scribd and Homejoy trialling the catering program since January 2014, with revenue up 35 percent week over week after launch.

identity.mascot_or_character: Catering Captains (staff who deliver and serve meals) act as a brand character of sorts
identity.visual_style: Healthy, hospitality-led positioning; the company said it wanted to be the 'Whole Foods of food delivery' (2013 coverage)

rebrands.why: Not stated; renamed at general availability in San Francisco with a new app

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive friendly name and a named service-staff concept, but no press about the brand itself or community found.

pivots.from: Consumer healthy food delivery (launched as Hasty, renamed Zesty 2013-11)
pivots.why: Trialled from January 2014 with startup customers and fast early growth per TechCrunch 2014-03.

outcome_analysis: Zesty moved from consumer delivery to office catering during YC W14 and raised a 17M USD Series A in 2015, reaching about 20.7M USD total. By November 2016 TechCrunch reported the CEO had been replaced amid stiff competition from rivals such as ZeroCater and Farm Hill, and in April 2018 Square bought certain assets and about the team for Caviar for Teams, terms undisclosed. A labor-heavy, regional, copyable service never gained a lasting edge; no later round was found, so this reads as a stall followed by an asset sale.
notes: Seed of about 3.7M USD (Y Combinator, SV Angel) appears only in a search snippet, so it is not recorded as a round; total raised of 20.7M USD is stated by TechCrunch 2016 and The Spoon 2018, consistent with 17M plus roughly 3.7M. The 2013 competitors are for the original consumer delivery product; TechCrunch 2014 on the catering pivot named none, and ZeroCater and Farm Hill are named only in 2016, so they are described in outcome_analysis, not listed. Brand name origin not found. Unrelated companies Zesty.io and Zesty.co share the name.
